title: Paul Walks Into Danger in Jerusalem
overview: Paul hears repeated warnings from friends who love him and still goes on to Jerusalem, where a false rumor sparks a riot and Roman soldiers arrest him.

parts.label: Tearful goodbyes at Tyre (vv. 1-6)
parts.note: Paul sails down the coast and stays a week with the believers in Tyre, who sense through the Spirit that trouble awaits him and beg him not to go. Many readers think the Spirit showed them the danger, while the plea to stay away came from their own love and worry.

parts.label: A prophet acts out a warning (vv. 7-14)
parts.note: At Philip's house the prophet Agabus ties himself up with Paul's belt, a dramatic sign like those of older Hebrew prophets, meaning Paul will be bound and handed over to the Romans. Paul answers his weeping friends that he is ready to be jailed or even die, and they stop pleading and leave it to the Lord's will.

parts.label: A rumor in the Jerusalem church (vv. 15-25)
parts.note: James, the church's leader, rejoices at Paul's report but warns that thousands of Jewish believers have heard Paul tells Jews abroad to abandon the law of Moses. He asks Paul to cover the costs for four men finishing a vow, likely a temporary religious promise ending with shaved heads and temple offerings, to show he still honors the law.

parts.label: A false charge in the temple (vv. 26-29)
parts.note: During the purification days, visitors from the province of Asia accuse Paul of bringing a non-Jew into the inner temple courts, which was forbidden on pain of death. The charge was only a guess, because they had seen him in the city with Trophimus, a man from Ephesus.

parts.label: Riot and arrest (vv. 30-36)
parts.note: A mob drags Paul out and beats him until the Roman commander from the fortress beside the temple rushes in and chains him, much as Agabus predicted. Christians have often noticed that the crowd's shout to be rid of him echoes the crowd at Jesus' trial.

parts.label: Mistaken identity on the steps (vv. 37-40)
parts.note: The commander is surprised Paul speaks Greek, having taken him for an Egyptian rebel who had led a revolt into the wilderness, someone an ancient Jewish historian also mentions. Paul says he is a Jew from the respected city of Tarsus and addresses the crowd in their own tongue, which some translations call Hebrew but most scholars think was Aramaic, the everyday language of Jews there.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether Paul was faithfully following God by going to Jerusalem despite the warnings or was acting against good counsel, and on whether joining the temple vow was a wise gesture of peace or an uneasy compromise.
think: When people who care about you warn you away from something you feel you have to do, how do you decide whose judgment to trust?
